texts.facts: The present is a complaint filed under section 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (herein after referred to as Pfa Act), alleging that the accused have violated the provisions of t he PFA Act and Rules. Da vs Baldev Raj Etc. on 31 July, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75148564/ 1 2. As per the complaint, on 07.09.2009, the Food Inspector (herein after referred to as FI) Shri Hukum Singh and FA Balwant Shah under the supervision of Local Health Authority (herein after referred to as LHA)/SDM) Shri Rakesh Khanna visited the premises of M/s Miglani Super Store, 13/392, Geeta Colony, Delhi - 110031, where accused Baldev Raj was found conducting business of food articles including 'Milk Rusk'(ready for sale), having identical label declaration. The FI disclosed his identity and expressed his intention to purchase a sample of "Milk Rusk" from the vendor for analysis. The sample consisted of six sealed plastic packets each packet containing 180 g "Milk Rusk" taken as such in originally sealed condition and having identical label declaration as it is reproduced on notice in Form -IV. The sample was taken under the supervision/ direction of Sh. Rakesh Khanna SDM/LHA. The Food Inspector divided the sample into three equal parts then and there by putting two sealed plastic packets of the Milk Rusks as one counter part of the sample. Each bottle containing the sample was separately packed, fastened and sealed according to PFA Act and Rules. The vendor's signatures were obtained on the LHA slip and the wrapper of the sample. Notice was given to accused Baldev Raj and the price of sample DA vs Baldev Raj etc. was also offered to him vide receipt dated 07.09.2009. Notice in Form-VI was also prepared in the name of supplier firm M/s Bakewell, Bakers, H No. 3B, Street No. 16, Sarojani Park, Shastri Nagar, Delhi - 31. Panchnama too was prepared at the spot. All the documents prepared by FI were signed by accused Baldev Raj and the other witness Sh. Balwant Shah FA. Before starting sample proceeding efforts were made to join public witnesses but none came forward, as such Sh.Balwant Shah, FA was joined as witness. 3. One counter-part of the sample bearing LHA Code No. 21/LHA/26283 was also sent to Public Analyst, Delhi in intact condition and remaining two counter-parts were deposited with the SDM/LHA in intact condition. Public Analyst analysed the sample and found the same to be misbranded. The report of the Public Analyst is as follows: "The sample is misbranded because there is violation of Rule 32 (e)(f) and the language of best before declaration is not as per Rule 32(i) of PFA Act and Rule. However, the same is not adulterated." 4. It is the case of the complainant that accused No. 1 Baldev Raj was the vendor-cum-proprietor of M/s Miglani Super Store, 13/392, Geeta Colony, Delhi - 110031 at the time of taking sample as such he is incharge of and responsible for day to day conduct of the business of the said shop. The sample article of the food 'Milk Rusk' was manufactured by M/s Bakewell Bakers, H.No. 3B, Gali No.16, Sarojini Park, Shastri Nagar, New Delhi DA vs Baldev Raj etc. and supplied to M/s Miglani Super Store. M/s Miglani Super Store is a proprietorship concern and accused No. 2 Rajender Kumar is the proprietor of the said firm and as such he is incharge of and responsible for day to day conduct of the business. Da vs Baldev Raj Etc. on 31 July, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75148564/ 2 5. Thereafter on completion of investigation, sanction under section 20 of the PFA Act was obtained from the Director PFA. The complaint was then filed in the Court on 29.03.2010 alleging violation of section 2 (ix)(k) of PFA Act, 1954 and Rule 32(e)(f)&(i) of PFA Rules, 1955, which is punishable under Section 16(1)(a) read with Section 7 of the PFA Act, 1954 by the accused. 6. As the complaint was filed in writing by a public servant, recording of pre-summoning evidence was dispensed with and the accused was summoned vide order dated 29.03.2010. Based on the report of the PA, notice was framed against the accused for commission of the offence punishable under section 7/16(1) (a) PFA Act being violation of Section 2 (ix)(k) of PFA Act, 1954 and Rule 32(e)(f)&(i) of PFA Rules, to which accused pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. 7. At the trial, the prosecution examined three witness in support of its case. PW-1 SDM/LHA Sh Rakesh Khanna, PW-2 FI Hukum Singh, PW-3 FA Balwant Sah . PW-2 and PW-3 were part of the team that had visited the spot for sample proceedings under the supervision of SDM/LHA Sh Rakesh Khanna. These witness narrated the steps undertaken by them during the sample proceedings, including disclosing their identity, expressing DA vs Baldev Raj etc. intention to purchase sample for analysis, lifting the six sample of "Milk Rusk" lying in sealed packets of 180 gms each, bearing identical label declaration, dividing it into three counter parts by putting two such packets together as one counterparts, separately sealing, packing and marking the same and obtaining signatures of vendor and witnesses. They also proved the necessary documents including the vendor's receipt Ex.PW-1/A, Notice Ex.PW-1/B, Notice u/s 14 A Ex.PW1/C and Panchnama Ex. PW- 1/D. The vendor also handed over photocopy of bill of purchase Mark-X, copy of MCD license Mark X-1 and copy of driving license mark X-2. Thereafter, on the next working day i.e. 08.09.2009, one counterpart alongwith a copy of Memo in Form VII in a sealed packet and another copy of Memo in Form VII in a separate sealed cover were deposited with PA vide PA's Receipt Ex. PW-2/A and the remaining two counterparts alongwith two copies of Memo in Form VII in a sealed packet were deposited with LHA on 08.09.2009 vide LHA Receipt Ex. PW-1/E, under intimation that one counterpart of the sample has already been deposited with the PA. Thereafter, PA Report Ex. PW-1/F was received through LHA, which revealed that the sample was misbranded and accordingly on the directions of SDM / LHA, PW- 2 FI Hukam Singh started the investigation. During investigation, PW-2 FI Hukam Singh sent a letter Ex.PW-2/B to VAT Officer, Ward No.80, regarding the constitution of M/s Miglani Super Store. PW-2 FI Hukam Singh also sent letters dated 29.10.2009, 11.11.2009, 14.12.2009 and 24.12.2009 Ex.PW-2/C to Ex.PW- 2/F to M/s Bakewell Bakers, H.No. 3B, Gali No.16, Sarojini Park, Shastri Nagar, New Delhi and received reply Ex. PW-2/G. PW-2 DA vs Baldev Raj etc. FI Hukam Singh also received copy of Voter ID Mark 2/1 and copy of certificate of registration from Weight and Measures Department, NCT Delhi, in the name of M/s Bakewell Bakers Mark 2/2. Thereafter PW-2 FI Hukam Singh sent letters Ex. PW- 2/H to VAT Officer, Ward no.80 regarding the constitution of M/s Bakewell Bakers. Thereafter after completion of investigation, PW-2 FI Hukam Singh put the entire case file before the concerned SDM / LHA Sh. D.P.Singh, who forwarded the same to the then Director PFA for obtaining his Consent and the then Director PFA Shri K.R.Kishore granted his Consent for prosecution of accused persons after applying his mind vide Ex. PW-2/I. Then, PW-2 FI Hukam Singh filed the complaint Ex. PW 2/J before this Court. Then, intimation letter Ex.PW2/K alongwith copies of PA Report were sent to the accused persons through registered post Mark-2/3 which were not received back undelivered. These Da vs Baldev Raj Etc. on 31 July, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75148564/ 3 witnesses were duly cross-examined by Ld. Defence Counsel. 8. Statement of the accused under section 313 CrPC were recorded on 05.05.2017 wherein the accused denied the allegations and pleaded innocence. Thereafter, the matter was fixed for defence evidence. 9. In their defence, accused No. 1 Baldev Raj examined himself as DW-1. Thereafter, the defence evidence was closed and the matter was fixed for final arguments.
